# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)

Diagnosed the champion cand_0002's trials from `./trajectories/` (33 trials, 11 val tasks). **Exactly 1 imperfect trial exists**: case-030-real-operator-structured-logging t0 (task mean 0.92; t1/t2 score 5/5). All 32 other trials score full. No ENVIRONMENT faults. Max recoverable ≈ +0.008 val (0.992 → 1.0).

Context from the handover: five prior iterations (cand_0003/0005/0006/0007/0008) targeted this same trial and were all threshold-REJECTED with `broke={}` — the edits did no measurable damage but did not clear the 0.3·SE noise bar. cand_0008 (the strongest prior design: shape-level enforcement of the epic shape, not just its recording) had its diff.patch truncated at copy, so its edits had to be reconstructed from its PROCESS.md. Per the framework's repeated gate note ("keep the edits that produced the fixed tasks as your starting point; do not rewrite them") this iteration re-derives and re-ships that batch — a fresh-tag re-measure of the best-known edit set, not a new design.

| rank | cluster | task (trial) | shared root cause | tag | change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Review-driven work-type split of a shared-surface enforcement deliverable → unmanaged size overage + unrecorded bundling (dq 4/5) | case-030 (t0) | Internal review cycle 1 docked E001's size and issued a split suggestion; the revise executed the old "Oversized epic: Split by sub-deliverable" playbook entry by carving the CI lint rule into standalone E004 ("CI lint rule enforcing structured reconciliation log fields", same component as E001/E002). E001 stayed over the ~2-week guideline — the external grader docked exactly that ("the size remains above guideline, which the embedded adversarial review also docked") — plus the HLR-7 P1-into-P0 bundling recorded only as scattered prose, not on the matrix row. Passing siblings t1/t2 keep 3 epics with the lint rule divided per binary (t1's summary: "the DAG issue was resolved by making the lint coverage per-binary") and the bundling flagged in-row (t1) or as a self-contained Step-4 analysis (t2) — shapes the graders quote in their 5/5 rationales | BEHAVIORAL (churn instruction in the revise playbook) + KNOWLEDGE (recording contracts) | STRUCTURAL: validator check 6 (work-type-extracted enforcement deliverable → per-surface fold-back) + generation rule + review classification + revise playbook replacement |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)

All 9 edits target cluster 1 (the only failing cluster). Structurally this is cand_0008's design (reconstructed from its PROCESS.md, its diff.patch being truncated): the epic SHAPE is enforced in code at every phase where the extraction could appear — decompose (Step 8c precondition), review (Step 1.7), and revise (Step 4 re-run, the phase where t0's E004 was actually created).

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/new-rule now does on those exact inputs)

- **Validator check 6** — `--self-check` passes (6 checks fire on the bad fixture, clean on the good; new fixtures cover both polarities: standalone lint-rule epic with same-component siblings fires; a lone enforcement-tool epic — the component's only implementation work — passes). Simulated end-to-end on t0's reconstructed final shape (E001 "Manager binary reconciliation log standardization" + E002 "Cloudmanager binary reconciliation log standardization" + E004 "CI lint rule enforcing structured reconciliation log fields", all component "OpenShift AI Productization", plus the docs epic): exits 1 with "RHAISTRAT-8010-E004.md: standalone enforcement deliverable … FIX: fold the enforcement work back into every epic whose surface it covers". On t1's passing 3-epic shape (no E004): clean.
- **trace case-030 t0 (review cycle 1: "one minor issue: E001 oversized. Fixed by splitting the CI lint rule into E004"; grader: "the size remains above guideline, which the embedded adversarial review also docked")** → the chain is now broken at three points: (i) review Criterion 3's classification forbids the un-actionable split suggestion and demands the trigger/fold-back corrections instead; (ii) if a split is nevertheless attempted, revise Step 4's validator run exits 1 on the standalone lint epic and the new playbook entry folds it back per surface — the t1 5/5 shape, which t1's summary explicitly documents ("the lint coverage per-binary, each implementation epic authors and verifies the lint"); (iii) the kept-overage path now records estimate + rationale + re-split trigger, the shape the t2 grader quoted at 5/5 ("records a concrete re-split trigger if the audit exceeds the 75% estimate. This is a defensible trade-off, not a monolith gap").
- **trace case-030 t0 (grader: HLR-7 bundling recorded only in prose)** → Step 4's row-flag contract + review Criterion 3's bundling-recording check (minor) + the revise's "record in matrix row" correction land the `(bundled)` flag + inline rationale — exactly t1's matrix row the t1 grader quoted at 5/5. t0 is the only trial whose bundling lives solely in scattered prose.
- **Blast radius (all edits, BOUNDED)**: every edit fires only under a discriminator — enforcement-titled general epic with same-component non-docs Implementation siblings (corpus title scan: no passing trial's epic set contains one; t1/t2 have no standalone epic), kept overage (only t0), kept bundling recorded off-row (only t0). Passing tasks in the class: case-013/014/015/016/017/018/019/020/024/029 and case-030 t1/t2; none produces a shape any new rule flags or demands changed.

## Process & features used

- Serial (no subagents/worktrees): a single failing cluster with one coherent mechanism; the 9 edits span 4 files whose contents must stay mutually consistent (validator ↔ decompose Step 4/5/6.5/8c ↔ review 1.7/Criterion 3 ↔ revise playbook) — parallel edit-subagents would have conflicted.
- Read: `guidance/skill-package/SKILL.md` (levers: skipped-step→bundled-script, output-contract, worked example), JOURNAL RESULT lines for all 8 prior iterations, rejected.jsonl (via journal), `prior_iterations/cand_0008/PROCESS.md` (the design reconstructed — its diff.patch is truncated at DIAGNOSIS.json).
- Improvement types applied (multiple): bundled-script enforcement (validator check 6), generation rule + worked example (Step 5 sub-bullet), output-contract recording rules (Step 4 / Step 6.5), review-to-revise issue mapping with severity calibration (Step 1.7 / Criterion 3), revise-playbook classified replacement (churn-instruction removal).

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)

- The validator's checks 1–5 (judge parity) and their decompose-8c / review-1.7 / revise-4 wiring — unchanged this iteration.
- Check 6's four-part discriminator (general type + enforcement TITLE + same-component sibling + not-the-only-implementation-work). Broadening it to body-text matching or dropping the sibling condition would risk false positives on passing trials.
- The Criterion 3 heterogeneous-monolith split demand (case-029 t0 relies on it).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)

- Grader-side dq 4-vs-5 variance beyond the two named gaps — no prompt defect to fix; the shape/recording contracts are the strongest available lever (same conclusion as the cand_0003/0005/0006/0007/0008 handovers).
- Mandated-AC (Rules 24/25) validator prep — that judge is staged thresholdless; not REAL.
- Any change to SKILL.md dispatch/wave logic, fetch-agent.md — no failures in those phases.
- New mechanisms beyond cand_0008's design — six threshold-rejections on this trial with `broke={}` say the honest read is measurement-limited-at-ceiling; adding novel speculative edits on top would only add regression risk, so this batch re-ships the strongest prior design under a fresh tag.

## Environment faults

None. All 33 trials ran to completion; the single failure is a capability failure.
